lines: Sudden onset severe pain, redness, and swelling in left knee over 2 days

encounters.cc: Acute left calf swelling and throbbing pain after 12-hour international flight

lines: Acute left calf swelling and throbbing pain after 12-hour international flight
This 68-year-old female with chronic kidney disease stage 3b, obesity class II, and prior lower extremity swelling presents with acute left calf complaints.
She describes the pain as throbbing, worsened with walking, and accompanied by tightness in the lower leg.
She has no history of recent trauma but reports that she recently returned from a 12-hour international flight two days ago.
She denies chest pain, shortness of breath, or hemoptysis.
- Pseudogout (Acute Calcium Pyrophosphate Dihydrate Crystal Deposition Disease) (diagnosed 2021-07-15)
- Gastroesophageal reflux disease with paraesophageal hiatal hernia
She has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus, both of which are well controlled on medication.
- Left knee arthroscopy with debridement (10 years prior)
- Insulin glargine 18 units subcutaneously at bedtime
- Acetaminophen 500 mg PO every 6 hours as needed for joint pain
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 12 years ago, 20 pack-year history.
Alcohol: Rare, 1-2 glasses of wine monthly.
Physical examination reveals unilateral left leg swelling with pitting edema extending up to the knee.
The left calf is tender to palpation, and there is a positive Homan sign.
The remainder of the physical exam is unremarkable.
Laboratory studies, including baseline coagulation parameters, are within normal limits.
Doppler ultrasound of the left lower extremity demonstrates non-compressibility of the proximal femoral vein consistent with acute deep vein thrombosis (DVT).
Given her risk of progression to pulmonary embolism, the medical team initiates treatment with fondaparinux.
The patient tolerates the therapy well without evidence of bleeding, and her leg pain improves with continued treatment and compression stockings.
